New Products.title: Visual Studio April Update: Cloud Agent Integration
New Products.description: April 2026 update centers on agentic workflows: cloud agent sessions launch directly from IDE, custom agents gain user-level support in %USERPROFILE%/.github/agents/, new Debugger agent validates fixes against live runtime behavior, customizable keyboard shortcuts, new chat history panel, and C++ code editing tools now generally available.

New Products.title: Week 17 Updates: UltraReview Research Preview
New Products.description: /ultrareview opens as a research preview, automatic session recaps when returning to terminal, custom color themes for plugins, redesigned web version with sessions sidebar and drag-and-drop layout, Vim visual mode support, hooks can call MCP tools, and performance improvements including 67% faster /resume on large sessions.

New Products.title: Devin 2.2 Release
New Products.description: Desktop support enabled by default for new users, existing users can enable through Settings, enhanced session management indicating 'Action Required' state, minor bug fixes and polish.

New Products.title: Version 2.1.128: Performance and UX Improvements
New Products.description: Bare /color picks random session color, /mcp shows tool count and flags empty servers, --plugin-dir accepts .zip archives, --channels works with console authentication, subprocesses no longer inherit OTEL environment variables, and multiple fixes for focus mode, drag-and-drop, and terminal rendering.

New Products.title: Aider v0.86.0: GPT-5 and Grok-4 Support
New Products.description: Added support for all GPT-5 models, added support for Grok-4 via xai/grok-4 and openrouter/x-ai/grok-4 model names, added support for gemini-2.5-flash-lite-preview-06-17 model, improved /clear and /undo commands, fixed settings replacement issue, and bumped dependencies to litellm 1.75.0.

New Products.title: Windsurf 2.0: Agent Command Center and Devin Integration
New Products.description: Introducing Windsurf 2.0 with the Agent Command Center, enabling local and cloud agents to work together. Features include Devin integration in Windsurf, enhanced collaborative AI capabilities, and improved agentic workflows for shipping code faster.

New Products.title: Team Marketplace Updates
New Products.description: Team marketplace enhancements for sharing custom extensions and tools across teams.

New Products.title: Build Programmatic Agents with the Cursor SDK
New Products.description: Introduction of the Cursor SDK for building programmatic agents, enabling developers to create custom agents and automate workflows.

New Products.title: Version v0.42.0-nightly.20260504
New Products.description: Nightly release with workspace trust documentation updates, ACP client modularization, test fixes, /exit --delete flag for session deletion, @ mention gemini robot support, API timeout reduction to 60s with retries, InvalidStream event handling, GitHub App token for CI, logPrompts flag respect, API key validation fixes, exit_plan_mode shell protection, GrepTool case-sensitivity fixes, Gemma setup guide, non-https proxy URL support, productivity optimizations, ACP prompt turn processing delegation, platform-specific undo/redo for WSL, byte length limits for stdin, shell tool header wrapping, voice mode UI updates, /commands list subcommand, extension delete alias, and numerous bug fixes and improvements.

New Products.title: Version 0.128.0
New Products.description: Major release adding persisted /goal workflows with app-server APIs, model tools, runtime continuation, and TUI controls. Features include codex update command, configurable TUI keymaps, plan-mode nudges, action-required terminal titles, active-turn /statusline and /title edits, expanded permission profiles with built-in defaults, sandbox CLI profile selection, improved plugin workflows with marketplace installation, external agent session import, MultiAgentV2 configuration improvements, resume/interruption fixes, TUI reliability improvements, managed network hardening, Windows sandbox and PTY fixes, Bedrock model support fixes, and MCP/plugin edge case handling.

New Products.title: AI Programming Platform 2.0 Launches with Multi-Agent Collaboration
New Products.description: Major AI programming platforms are launching 2.0 versions with multi-agent collaboration systems, improving complex problem-solving accuracy by 30%. Cursor, developed by Anysphere and built on VS Code, leads with deep AI integration throughout the development workflow.
New Products.author: Platform Updates

New Products.title: Version 2.1.132 Released
New Products.description: Claude Code v2.1.132 released with multiple bug fixes and improvements including session ID environment variable, alternate screen opt-out, improved SIGINT handling, terminal fixes for various IDEs (Cursor, VS Code, JetBrains), and MCP server error handling improvements.

community_feedback.quote: I'm using both claude code (opus-4.7) and codex (gpt-5.5). The agents are perfectly capable of delivering most features hands free these days, but the code quality is still miserable without another few rounds of prompt.
community_feedback.source: Hacker News - How to improve code quality of Claude Code (May 2026)

community_feedback.quote: staying human-in-the-loop, more upfront prompt effort, more/better instructions, starting to look at agent teams/workflows
community_feedback.source: Hacker News - How to improve code quality of Claude Code (May 2026)

community_feedback.quote: Claude Code refuses requests or charges extra if your commits mention OpenClaw - users experiencing billing issues when certain keywords appear in their codebase
community_feedback.source: Hacker News - Claude Code billing/keyword filtering discussion (May 2026)

community_feedback.quote: I upgraded to 2.1.32 just to try Opus 4.6, but after upgrading it has been full of issues. /compact is not working at all. It asks me to go back to a previous message, and when I do that and run /compact, it just gets stuck at 0 tokens. In general it also feels much slower.
I am also not sure if this is a Claude Code version issue or a model issue, but I am noticing that Opus 4.6 consumes a lot more of my 5-hour usage limit compared to what I normally see.

New Products.title: Context Usage Breakdown
New Products.description: Cursor 3.3 introduces context usage breakdown feature allowing developers to see detailed stats about their agent's context consumption across rules, skills, MCPs, and subagents to diagnose issues and optimize setup.

New Products.title: Enterprise-Managed Plugins in GitHub Copilot CLI Public Preview
New Products.description: GitHub Copilot CLI introduces enterprise-managed plugins in public preview, allowing organizations to control and manage CLI plugin access and configuration for their teams.

New Products.title: Version 2.2.17 - Devin Review & Quick Review Integration
New Products.description: Windsurf IDE v2.2.17 released with Devin Review and Quick Review now available to all users, Agent Command Center improvements with list display, better session sorting/filtering, and Windows update bug fixes.

New Products.title: Main Branch Updates - Claude 4.5/4.6 and GPT-5 Support
New Products.description: Aider main branch adds support for Claude 4.5/4.6 models with updated aliases, expanded Gemini model support (2.5 Flash, Flash-Lite, Gemini 3 preview), DeepSeek Reasoner model, and new OpenAI GPT-5.1/5.2/5.3/5.4 models across providers.

New Products.title: Version 1.3.38 - Config File Support & Workspace Filtering
New Products.description: Continue v1.3.38 introduces .continue/configs support, workspace directory session history filtering, config.yaml existence checks, and multiple dependency updates including happy-dom and handlebars.

New Products.title: Model Controls, Spend Management, and Usage Analytics
New Products.description: Cursor releases enterprise admin updates including granular model access controls at provider/model level, updated spend management, and enhanced usage analytics with option to block new providers by default.

New Products.title: Version 0.128.0 - Goals, Plugins, Multi-Agent V2 Improvements
New Products.description: Codex CLI 0.128.0 released with persisted /goal workflows, configurable TUI keymaps, plan-mode nudges, expanded permission profiles with sandbox controls, improved plugin workflows with marketplace installation, remote bundle caching, and MultiAgentV2 configuration enhancements including thread caps and wait-time controls.

New Products.title: Sensitive Toggle for Secrets & Multi-Edit Merging
New Products.description: Devin release April 24, 2026 introduces sensitive toggle for secrets (masked/visible), merged multi-edits in progress tab showing combined diffs, session category/subcategory in v3 API, and wide markdown tables in chat.

New Products.title: DecodingTrust-Agent Platform (DTap): A Controllable and Interactive Red-Teaming Platform for AI Agents
New Products.description: A comprehensive 279-page paper introducing DTap, a platform for red-teaming AI agents. This addresses critical safety and security concerns as AI agents become more capable and autonomous, particularly relevant for AI coding agents that interact with production systems.
New Products.author: Zhaorun Chen, Xun Liu, Haibo Tong, et al.

New Products.title: Devin Review & Quick Review Available
New Products.description: All Windsurf IDE users now have access to Devin Review and Quick Review features with their existing subscription. Added list display option for agent inbox, improved sessions sidebar sorting and filtering, and performance improvements for loading and switching sessions.

New Products.title: Rubber Duck CLI Now Supports More Models
New Products.description: Rubber Duck feature in GitHub Copilot CLI now supports additional models beyond the initial offering, expanding debugging and code explanation capabilities.

New Products.title: v2.1.128 Release
New Products.description: Latest Claude Code release with random session colors, MCP tool counts, plugin zip support, console channels for API key auth, model picker cleanup, OTEL isolation improvements, and numerous bug fixes.

community_feedback.quote: I use Claude Code for work every day. Honestly, after seeing the v2.1.128 update yesterday, I got chills. Not because the update was flashy, but because all three bugs it fixed were ones I encountered personally.

New Products.title: Week 19 Updates: Plugin System Enhancements & Command History
New Products.description: Load plugins from .zip archives and URLs, expanded plugin directory support, global command history search across projects using Ctrl+R, and Git worktree support with branch creation from local repositories.

New Products.title: PR Review, Build Plan in Parallel, and Split PRs
New Products.description: New PR review experience with inline review threads, commits tab, and changes tab. Build in parallel from plans using async subagents. Split changes into PRs with quick action. Pin skills as quick actions. Context usage breakdown.

community_feedback.quote: Reports of teams reducing code review time from 45 minutes to 10 minutes using Cursor's AI review commands.
Multiple reports about Cursor having too many bugs. Performance issues with large codebases (can be slow or freeze).

New Products.title: Aider v0.56.0
New Products.description: Enables prompt caching for Sonnet via OpenRouter, 8k output tokens for Sonnet via VertexAI and DeepSeek V2.5, new /report command for GitHub Issues, --chat-language switch, and numerous bug fixes.

community_feedback.quote: There's a GitHub issue (#1507) about Windows installation difficulties with Aider v0.56.0

New Products.title: Shareable Agents and Code Review Inbox
New Products.description: You can now generate publicly shareable links to your agents so that others can try out your workflows. Continue's pull request inbox helps you ship code faster and with higher quality. You can filter by pull requests you've opened or that are assigned to you.

New Products.title: OpenAI launched a Codex extension for Chrome
New Products.description: OpenAI has released a Chrome extension for Codex that allows it to use Chrome on your computer to complete work inside websites and apps where you're already signed in. The extension works in task-specific tab groups, enabling developers to maintain productivity while automating workflows across multiple web applications.
New Products.author: Jay Peters

New Products.title: Anthropic Launches the World's First 'Hybrid Reasoning' AI Model
New Products.description: Anthropic has unveiled what it claims is the first 'hybrid reasoning' AI model, combining different types of reasoning approaches to improve performance on complex tasks. The model represents an evolution in AI architecture that could impact how developers approach building AI-powered applications requiring sophisticated logical reasoning.
New Products.author: Will Knight

New Products.title: Copilot CLI May Update and Model Deprecations
New Products.description: Path completion improvements in /add-dir, slash commands can now appear mid-input, and bug fixes. Announced deprecation of Grok Code Fast 1, GPT-5.2, and GPT-5.2-Codex models. Copilot code review comment types now in usage metrics API.

community_feedback.quote: Starting June 1, 2026, GitHub is moving Copilot from request-based billing to usage-based billing - users would naturally be a little upset.
GitHub Copilot's shift to a paid model exposes the 'biggest lie' in developer tools pricing.

New Products.title: Gemini CLI v0.40.0 - Offline Search and Advanced Resource Management
New Products.description: Bundled ripgrep for offline search support and added GitHub-style colorblind themes. Introduced MCP resource tools and transitioned to a prompt-driven, four-tier memory management system. Enabled topic update narrations by default and streamlined Gemma local model setup.

New Products.title: SkillOS: Learning Skill Curation for Self-Evolving Agents
New Products.description: ICML 2026 accepted paper introducing a system for curating and evolving skills in AI agents. The SkillOS framework enables agents to learn and organize skills dynamically, supporting continuous improvement and specialization. This has implications for AI coding agents that need to adapt to new programming paradigms and frameworks.
New Products.author: Siru Ouyang, Jun Yan, et al.

New Products.title: Rate Limits Doubled for Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise Plans
New Products.description: On May 6, 2026, Claude Code five-hour rate limits were doubled for Pro, Max, Team, and seat-based Enterprise plans, with peak-hours throttling also addressed.

community_feedback.quote: Anthropic announced doubling of 5-hour rate limits for Pro, Max, Team, and Enterprise plans, removal of peak hours limits
Users discussing hitting 20% of weekly limits in just 2 hours before the increase

New Products.title: Version 3.3 Bug Fixes
New Products.description: May 6, 2026 update (v3.3) fixed various cloud agent timing and hydration edge cases affecting reliability, plus performance improvements.

New Products.title: Copilot Code Review Billing Changes (Effective June 1, 2026)
New Products.description: GitHub announced changes to Copilot code review billing where each review will be billed as AI usage and start consuming GitHub Actions minutes.

New Features.title: Image AI Models Now Drive App Growth, Beating Chatbot Upgrades
New Features.description: Appfigures report finds that image model releases generate 6.5x more downloads than traditional model updates. Gemini's Nano Banana drove 22+ million downloads in 28 days (4x lift), while ChatGPT added 12M+ installs after GPT-4o image model. However, download spikes don't always convert to revenue - only ChatGPT successfully converted image model attention to $70M in consumer spending, while Gemini generated only $181K and Meta AI's Vibes saw no meaningful revenue.
New Features.author: Sarah Perez

New Features.title: Salvatore Sanfilippo Adds Array Data Type to Redis with AI Assistance
New Features.description: Redis creator Salvatore Sanfilippo submitted a PR adding a new array data type to Redis with 17 new commands (ARCOUNT, ARDEL, ARGET, etc.). The most interesting is ARGREP for server-side grep using the TRE regex library. Simon built an interactive playground for testing the new commands using Claude Code.
New Features.author: Simon Willison

New Features.title: 'This is Fine' Creator Says AI Startup Artisan Stole His Art
New Features.description: KC Green, creator of the 'This is fine' meme, says AI startup Artisan used his art in subway ads without permission. The ads feature the smiling dog surrounded by flames saying 'my pipeline is on fire' and urge passersby to 'Hire Ava the AI BDR.' Green told followers to 'please vandalize it if and when you see it' and said 'it's been stolen like AI steals.' Artisan previously courted controversy with billboards urging businesses to 'Stop hiring humans.'
New Features.author: Anthony Ha

New Features.title: Building Wildlife Sightings Feature with Claude Code on Mobile
New Features.description: Simon Willison built a new wildlife sightings feature for his blog entirely on his phone using Claude Code for web. The feature integrates iNaturalist observations, displays photos with species names, and includes search and filtering. He back-populated over a decade of wildlife observations including lemur photos from Madagascar 2019.
New Features.author: Simon Willison

New Features.title: OpenAI Codex CLI 0.128.0 Adds /goal Feature for Agentic Loops
New Features.description: OpenAI's Codex CLI added a /goal feature implementing a 'Ralph loop' - the agent keeps iterating until it completes the goal or exhausts the token budget. The feature is primarily implemented through goals/continuation.md and goals/budget_limit.md system prompts.
New Features.author: Simon Willison

New Features.title: Live blog: Code w/ Claude 2026
New Features.description: Simon Willison's live coverage of Anthropic's Code w/ Claude 2026 event. Key announcements: API volume up 17x YoY, increased rate limits for Claude Code (doubling for Pro/Max/Enterprise), SpaceX Colossus partnership for capacity, new Claude Managed Agent features (multi-agent orchestration, Outcomes, and 'Dreaming' for self-improvement), Claude Code Routines for async automation, CI auto-fix for PRs. Notable: Shopify and Mercado Libre targeting 90% autonomous coding by Q3 2026.
New Features.author: Simon Willison

New Features.title: iNaturalist sightings feature built entirely on phone with Claude Code
New Features.description: Simon Willison built a wildlife sightings feature for his blog using Claude Code for web, entirely on his phone while camping. The feature integrates with iNaturalist to display bird and wildlife photos with filters and search. Demonstrates the portability and capability of modern AI coding tools for full-stack development.
New Features.author: Simon Willison

New Features.title: Gmail's 'Help me write' AI tool will draft emails that sound more like you
New Features.description: Google is rolling out an update to Gmail's 'Help me write' AI feature that generates emails personalized to your tone and writing style. The tool can now pull in relevant context from Google Drive and Gmail history, making AI-generated communications more authentic and contextually relevant.
New Features.author: Jay Peters

New Features.title: Snap says its relationship with Perplexity ended 'amicably'
New Features.description: Snap ended its AI search partnership with Perplexity, noting in its Q1 2026 investor letter that analysts should not expect any contribution from Perplexity in revenue guidance. The AI search engine was originally intended to power Snap's AI features, but the company remains committed to 'intelligent eyewear' with more Specs news expected in June.
New Features.author: Victoria Song

New Technologies.title: Standing on the Shoulders of Giants: Stabilized Knowledge Distillation for Cross-Language Code Clone Detection
New Technologies.description: Research on stabilized knowledge distillation for cross-language code clone detection, addressing challenges in detecting similar code across different programming languages. 38 pages.
New Technologies.author: Mohamad Khajezade, Fatemeh H. Fard, Mohamed Sami Shehata

New Technologies.title: HAAS: A Policy-Aware Framework for Adaptive Task Allocation Between Humans and AI Systems
New Technologies.description: Framework for adaptive task allocation between humans and AI systems with policy awareness. Addresses human-AI collaboration and task distribution challenges.
New Technologies.author: Vicente Pelechano, Antoni Mestre, Manoli Albert, Miriam Gil

New Technologies.title: U-Define: Designing User Workflows for Hard and Soft Constraints in LLM-Based Planning
New Technologies.description: Research on designing user workflows for handling hard and soft constraints in LLM-based planning systems. Explores human-computer interaction challenges with LLM planning agents.
New Technologies.author: Christine P Lee, Xinyu Jessica Wang, Aws Albarghouthi, David Porfirio, Bilge Mutlu

New Technologies.title: Foundation-Model-Based Agents in Industrial Automation: Purposes, Capabilities, and Open Challenges
New Technologies.description: Comprehensive analysis of foundation-model-based agents in industrial automation, comparing classical agent applications with modern foundation models. 35 pages, 8 figures. Discusses purposes, capabilities, and open challenges.
New Technologies.author: Vincent Henkel, Felix Gehlhoff, David Kube, et al.

New Technologies.title: On Training Large Language Models for Long-Horizon Tasks: An Empirical Study of Horizon Length
New Technologies.description: Empirical study accepted at ICML 2026 on training LLMs for long-horizon tasks, examining how horizon length affects model performance. Research addresses challenges in multi-step reasoning and planning.
New Technologies.author: Sunghwan Kim, Junhee Cho, Beong-woo Kwak, et al.

New Technologies.title: Strategy-Aware Optimization Modeling with Reasoning LLMs
New Technologies.description: Research on strategy-aware optimization modeling using reasoning LLMs. Explores how language models can handle optimization problems with strategic considerations.
New Technologies.author: Ruiqing Zhao, Fengzhi Li, Yuan Zuo, et al.

New Technologies.title: DataClaw: A Process-Oriented Agent Benchmark for Exploratory Real-World Data Analysis
New Technologies.description: Introduction of DataClaw, a process-oriented agent benchmark designed for exploratory real-world data analysis. Provides framework for evaluating AI agents on complex data analysis tasks.
New Technologies.author: Qiaohong Zhang, Weihao Ye, Jialong Chen, et al.

New Technologies.title: Shadow-Loom: Causal Reasoning over Graphical World Model of Narratives
New Technologies.description: Shadow-Loom system for causal reasoning over graphical world models of narratives. 7 pages (28 pages total). Addresses challenge of understanding causality in narrative contexts.
New Technologies.author: David Wilmot

New Technologies.title: Position: How can Graphs Help Large Language Models?
New Technologies.description: Position paper examining how graph structures can enhance large language models. Accepted by Frontiers of Computer Science. Explores synergies between graph-based reasoning and LLMs.
New Technologies.author: Xiyuan Wang, Yi Hu, Yanbo Wang, Chuan Shi, Muhan Zhang

New Technologies.title: FitText: Evolving Agent Tool Ecologies via Memetic Retrieval
New Technologies.description: Research on FitText, a system for evolving agent tool ecologies through memetic retrieval. Explores how AI agents can dynamically develop and refine their tool capabilities.
New Technologies.author: Kyle Zheng, Han Zhang, Renliang Sun, et al.

New Technologies.title: The Compliance Trap: How Structural Constraints Degrade Frontier AI Metacognition Under Adversarial Pressure
New Technologies.description: Analysis of how structural constraints and compliance requirements can degrade frontier AI metacognitive capabilities under adversarial pressure. 9 pages, includes code and dataset.
New Technologies.author: Rahul Kumar

New Technologies.title: HeavySkill: Heavy Thinking as the Inner Skill in Agentic Harness
New Technologies.description: HeavySkill framework treating heavy thinking as an inner skill in agentic harness systems. 18 pages, 10 figures. Explores how to effectively harness and control deep reasoning capabilities in AI agents.
New Technologies.author: Jianing Wang, Linsen Guo, Zhengyu Chen, et al.

New Technologies.title: A Compound AI Agent for Conversational Grant Discovery
New Technologies.description: Introduction of a compound AI agent designed for conversational grant discovery. Accepted as demo submission to ACM CAIS. Explores multi-agent systems for information discovery tasks.
New Technologies.author: Zhisheng Tang, Mayank Kejriwal

New Technologies.title: EngiAgent: Fully Connected Coordination of LLM Agents for Solving Open-ended Engineering Problems with Feasible Solutions
New Technologies.description: EngiAgent system for fully connected coordination of LLM agents to solve open-ended engineering problems with feasible solutions. Accepted at ICML 2026. Explores multi-agent coordination for complex engineering challenges.
New Technologies.author: Xiyuan Zhou, Ruixi Zou, Xinlei Wang, et al.

New Technologies.title: Towards Understanding Specification Gaming in Reasoning Models
New Technologies.description: Research towards understanding specification gaming in reasoning models. Explores how AI models might game specifications rather than truly solving intended problems.
New Technologies.author: Kei Nishimura-Gasparian, Robert McCarthy, David Lindner

New Technologies.title: Granite 4.1 3B SVG Pelican Gallery - Testing AI Model Quality
New Technologies.description: Simon Willison tested IBM's Granite 4.1 family of LLMs (Apache 2.0 licensed) by prompting 'Generate an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle' against different sized quantized variants. Found that results were less interesting than expected with no distinguishable pattern relating quality to size - all were pretty terrible at the task. The 3B model has 21 different GGUF encoded variants ranging from 1.2GB to 6.34GB.
New Technologies.author: Simon Willison

New Technologies.title: IBM Releases Granite 4.1 Family of Apache 2.0 LLMs
New Technologies.description: IBM released Granite 4.1 LLMs in 3B, 8B, and 30B sizes, all Apache 2.0 licensed. Simon Willison tested SVG generation capabilities of quantized variants using 'pelican riding a bicycle' prompts, finding that smaller models didn't necessarily perform worse than larger ones for this task.
New Technologies.author: Simon Willison

New Technologies.title: Anthropic Research: Claude Shows Sycophancy in 38% of Spirituality Conversations
New Technologies.description: Anthropic's research on sycophancy found that while Claude showed sycophantic behavior in only 9% of conversations overall, this jumped to 38% for spirituality topics and 25% for relationship discussions. The study used an automatic classifier measuring willingness to push back and give proportional praise.
New Technologies.author: Anthropic (via Simon Willison)

New Technologies.title: Zig's 'Contributor Poker' Philosophy: Betting on People, Not PRs
New Technologies.description: Loris Cro, Zig Software Foundation VP of Community, explains Zig's strict LLM ban as 'contributor poker' - you bet on the contributor, not the cards. The project values growing new contributors over landing perfect code. LLM assistance breaks this model because reviewing AI-written PRs doesn't help build trusted, long-term contributors.
New Technologies.author: Loris Cro (via Simon Willison)

New Technologies.title: LLM 0.32a0: Major Backwards-Compatible Refactor Released
New Technologies.description: Simon Willison released LLM 0.32a0, a major backwards-compatible refactor of his Python LLM library and CLI tool. The alpha includes consequential changes he's been working toward for a while. Fixed a bug where tool-calling conversations weren't correctly reinflated from SQLite.
New Technologies.author: Simon Willison

New Technologies.title: Natural Language Autoencoders: Turning Claude's Thoughts into Text
New Technologies.description: Anthropic research (91 points on HN) on natural language autoencoders that convert Claude's internal thoughts into text. This relates to making AI reasoning more interpretable, which is important for AI coding systems where understanding the model's reasoning process is valuable.
New Technologies.author: Anthropic

New Technologies.title: ProgramBench: Can language models rebuild programs from scratch?
New Technologies.description: An ArXiv paper discussed on HN (127 points) that benchmarks whether language models can rebuild programs from scratch. This is a relevant evaluation for AI coding agents, testing their ability to understand and recreate complete programs.
New Technologies.author: Various researchers

New Technologies.title: ZAYA1-8B matches DeepSeek-R1 on math with less than 1B active parameters
New Technologies.description: Discussion (72 points on HN) about ZAYA1-8B, a model that matches DeepSeek-R1 on math benchmarks with fewer than 1B active parameters. This reflects ongoing research into more efficient model architectures for AI coding and reasoning tasks.
New Technologies.author: firethering.com

New Technologies.title: LongSeeker: Elastic Context Orchestration for Long-Horizon Search Agents
New Technologies.description: A paper on elastic context orchestration for long-horizon search agents, addressing how to manage and optimize context windows for agents performing extended search tasks. Relevant to AI coding agents that need to maintain context over long sessions.
New Technologies.author: Yijun Lu, Rui Ye, Yuwen Du, Jiajun Wang, Songhua Liu, Siheng Chen

New Technologies.title: Executable World Models for ARC-AGI-3 in the Era of Coding Agents
New Technologies.description: This paper explores executable world models for the ARC-AGI-3 benchmark, specifically in the context of coding agents. It addresses how AI agents can build and execute world models to solve complex reasoning tasks, relevant to the advancement of AI coding systems.
New Technologies.author: Sergey Rodionov

New Technologies.title: Design Conductor 2.0: An agent builds a TurboQuant inference accelerator in 80 hours
New Technologies.description: A remarkable case study where an AI agent built a complete TurboQuant inference accelerator in just 80 hours. This demonstrates the growing capability of AI agents to design complex hardware systems, with implications for AI-assisted hardware and system-level programming.
New Technologies.author: The Verkor Team: Ravi Krishna, Suresh Krishna, David Chin

New Technologies.title: AgentTrust: Runtime Safety Evaluation and Interception for AI Agent Tool Use
New Technologies.description: This paper introduces AgentTrust, a system for runtime safety evaluation and interception of AI agent tool use. As AI coding agents gain access to more powerful tools and systems, runtime safety mechanisms become increasingly important.
New Technologies.author: Chenglin Yang

New Technologies.title: AuditRepairBench: A Paired-Execution Trace Corpus for Evaluator-Channel Ranking Instability in Agent Repair
New Technologies.description: A benchmark and dataset for evaluating agent repair systems, focusing on evaluator-channel ranking instability. This is relevant to debugging and improving AI coding agents that can self-repair or be repaired by other agents.
New Technologies.author: Yuelin Hu, Zhenbo Yu, Zhengxue Cheng, Wei Liu, Li Song

New Technologies.title: Delta-Based Neural Architecture Search: LLM Fine-Tuning via Code Diffs
New Technologies.description: This paper explores using code deltas (differences) for neural architecture search and LLM fine-tuning. The approach leverages the structure of code changes to optimize model architectures, relevant to improving AI coding models through better training methodologies.
New Technologies.author: Santosh Premi Adhikari, Radu Timofte, Dmitry Ignatov

New Technologies.title: Continual Knowledge Updating in LLM Systems: Learning Through Multi-Timescale Memory Dynamics
New Technologies.description: A paper on continual learning and knowledge updating for LLM systems using multi-timescale memory dynamics. This addresses the challenge of keeping AI coding agents up-to-date with the latest programming knowledge and best practices.
New Technologies.author: Andreas Pattichis, Constantine Dovrolis

New Technologies.title: CuBridge: An LLM-Based Framework for Understanding and Reconstructing High-Performance Attention Kernels
New Technologies.description: CuBridge introduces an LLM-based framework for understanding and reconstructing high-performance attention kernels, accepted to ACL 2026. This demonstrates how LLMs can be used to optimize and understand low-level performance-critical code, relevant to AI-assisted performance optimization.
New Technologies.author: Xing Ma, Yangjie Zhou, Wu Sun, et al.

New Technologies.title: The Impossibility Triangle of Long-Context Modeling
New Technologies.description: This paper (41 pages, 6 figures) explores fundamental trade-offs in long-context modeling for language models. As AI coding agents need to maintain increasingly large contexts (entire codebases, documentation, etc.), understanding these limitations is crucial for system design.
New Technologies.author: Yan Zhou

New Technologies.title: LCM: Lossless Context Management
New Technologies.description: A paper on lossless context management, addressing how to efficiently manage and compress context without losing information. Critical for AI coding agents that need to work with large codebases and maintain context across long sessions.
New Technologies.author: Clint Ehrlich, Theodore Blackman

New Technologies.title: KernelBench-X: A Comprehensive Benchmark for Evaluating LLM-Generated GPU Kernels
New Technologies.description: Introduces KernelBench-X, a benchmark for evaluating GPU kernels generated by LLMs. As AI coding agents are increasingly asked to write performance-critical code, having robust benchmarks for evaluating generated low-level code is essential.
New Technologies.author: Han Wang, Jintao Zhang, Kai Jiang, et al.

New Technologies.title: Adaptivity Under Realizability Constraints: Comparing In-Context and Agentic Learning
New Technologies.description: Compares in-context learning (what LLMs do naturally) with agentic learning (using tools and external systems). This distinction is fundamental to understanding when to use different approaches in AI coding systems.
New Technologies.author: Anastasis Kratsios, A. Martina Neuman, Philipp Petersen

New Technologies.title: Granite 4.1 3B SVG Pelican Gallery - IBM's New Apache 2.0 LLMs
New Technologies.description: IBM released Granite 4.1 family of LLMs (3B, 8B, 30B sizes) under Apache 2.0 license. Simon tested SVG generation capabilities across 21 different quantized variants and found results underwhelming - no clear correlation between model size and output quality for the pelican bicycle test.
New Technologies.author: Simon Willison

New Technologies.title: Behind the Scenes Hardening Firefox with Claude Mythos Preview
New Technologies.description: Coverage of Mozilla's use of Claude Mythos preview to identify and fix security vulnerabilities in Firefox. The article details how AI-generated security bug reports evolved from mostly unwanted 'slop' to high-quality findings, with Mozilla fixing 423 security bugs in April 2026 (up from 20-30 per month throughout 2025). This demonstrates a major advancement in AI-assisted security research.
New Technologies.author: Simon Willison

New Technologies.title: Mozilla is sharing more details about some of the 271 Firefox bugs identified by Claude Mythos Preview
New Technologies.description: Mozilla revealed that Anthropic's Claude Mythos Preview model helped identify 271 bugs in Firefox. Breaking from their usual practice of keeping bug reports private for months, Mozilla decided to publicly release details of some bug reports due to the extraordinary level of interest and urgency in AI-assisted security research.
New Technologies.author: Jay Peters

New Technologies.title: Granite 4.1 3B SVG Pelican Gallery experiment
New Technologies.description: Simon Willison tested IBM's Granite 4.1 family of LLMs (Apache 2.0 licensed in 3B, 8B, and 30B sizes) by prompting different quantized variants to generate an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle. The results showed no clear correlation between model size and output quality, with all variants producing poor results. This provides insight into current limitations of LLM visual generation capabilities.
New Technologies.author: Simon Willison

New Technologies.title: AI Co-Mathematician: Accelerating Mathematicians with Agentic AI
New Technologies.description: Paper submitted to arXiv on May 8, 2026, describing an AI system designed to collaborate with mathematicians. The paper explores how agentic AI can accelerate mathematical research by assisting with proof generation, conjecture formation, and literature review. Authors include researchers from Google DeepMind and various academic institutions.
New Technologies.author: Daniel Zheng, Ingrid von Glehn, et al.

New Technologies.title: From Agent Loops to Deterministic Graphs: Execution Lineage for Reproducible AI-Native Work
New Technologies.description: Paper submitted May 8, 2026, addressing reproducibility challenges in AI-native workflows. The authors propose moving from agent loops to deterministic graphs to enable better tracking and reproduction of AI-assisted work. This is particularly relevant for debugging and understanding AI coding agent behavior.
New Technologies.author: Josh Rosen, Seth Rosen

New Technologies.title: Beyond Task Success: Measuring Workflow Fidelity in LLM-Based Agentic Payment Systems
New Technologies.description: Paper accepted at AIDS4DF Workshop, PAKDD 2026, discussing evaluation metrics for AI agents beyond simple task completion. The authors argue for measuring 'workflow fidelity' - how well an agent follows intended processes - which is crucial for financial and other high-stakes applications of AI coding agents.
New Technologies.author: Donghao Huang, Joon Kiat Chua, Zhaoxia Wang

New Technologies.title: Automated Alignment is Harder Than You Think
New Technologies.description: Paper submitted May 8, 2026, examining challenges in automating AI alignment. The authors demonstrate fundamental difficulties in creating automated systems that can reliably align AI behavior with human values, with implications for AI coding tools that need to maintain safety and security while remaining useful.
New Technologies.author: Aleksandr Bowkis, Marie Davidsen Buhl, Jacob Pfau, Geoffrey Irving

New Technologies.title: Karpathy on 'From Vibe Coding to Agentic Engineering' at AI Ascent 2026
New Technologies.description: At AI Ascent 2026, Andrej Karpathy discussed how 'vibe coding' has evolved over the past year. He explained the shift from one-shot prompt coding toward agentic engineering workflows, noting that programming has become 'unrecognizable' compared to just a year ago. The talk covered code agents, AutoResearch, and what Karpathy calls the 'Loopy Era of AI.'
New Technologies.author: Andrej Karpathy

New Technologies.title: Granite 4.1 LLMs Released by IBM with Apache 2.0 License
New Technologies.description: IBM released the Granite 4.1 family of LLMs (3B, 8B, 30B sizes) under Apache 2.0 license. Simon Willison conducted an experiment testing 'Generate an SVG of a pelican riding a bicycle' across 21 different quantized variants ranging from 1.2GB to 6.34GB. Results showed no clear pattern relating model size to output quality - all performed poorly at the specific task.
New Technologies.author: Simon Willison

Others.title: LLM coding workflow going into 2026 - Hacker News Discussion
Others.description: Hacker News discussion about LLM coding workflows going into 2026. Users working on multi-step AI pipelines (like 3D mesh generation with validation stages) find that LLMs often skip edge cases or take suboptimal paths. Discussion examines whether AI coding provides real speedup and trade-offs between manual coding vs AI assistance.
Others.author: Hacker News Community

Others.title: SAP Bets $1.16B on 18-Month-Old German AI Lab Prior Labs
Others.description: SAP announced plans to acquire German AI startup Prior Labs for an undisclosed amount and invest €1 billion (approximately $1.16 billion) over four years. Prior Labs, founded just 18 months ago, focuses on tabular foundation models (TFMs) for structured data. The startup's TabPFN models have been downloaded over 3 million times. SAP also announced strict AI agent policies, prohibiting unauthorized agents like OpenClaw while allowing SAP-endorsed architectures including Nvidia's NemoClaw.
Others.author: Anna Heim

Others.title: Y Combinator's Stake in OpenAI: 0.6% Worth Over $5 Billion
Others.description: John Gruber reveals that Y Combinator owns approximately 0.6% of OpenAI, worth over $5 billion at OpenAI's current $852 billion valuation. This information was notably difficult to obtain despite being known to some investors.
Others.author: John Gruber (via Simon Willison)

Others.title: Claude Code Helps Build Python Bindings and Test Regular Expression Security
Others.description: Simon Willison used Claude Code to build experimental Python bindings for Ville Laurikari's TRE regular expression engine using ctypes, then tested malicious regex attacks. TRE handled attacks better than Python's standard library due to lack of backtracking support.
Others.author: Simon Willison

Others.title: iNaturalist Observation Clumping Tool Built with Claude Code on Phone
Others.description: While camping, Simon Willison built an entire iNaturalist observation 'clumper' tool on his phone using Claude Code. The tool groups observations by time and proximity (default: 2 hours and 5km), outputs to JSON hosted on GitHub, and includes a JavaScript viewer with modal image display.
Others.author: Simon Willison

Others.title: Meta Acquires Robotics Startup Assured Robot Intelligence for Humanoid AI
Others.description: Meta acquired humanoid robotics startup Assured Robot Intelligence (ARI) for an undisclosed sum. ARI's team, including co-founders Lerrel Pinto (formerly NYU) and Xiaolong Wang (formerly UCSD and Nvidia), will join Meta's Superintelligence Labs division. The startup was building foundation models for humanoid robots to perform physical labor. The acquisition reflects Meta's years-long ambition to build humanoid robots and the broader industry belief that AGI may require training AI models in the physical world.
Others.author: Julie Bort

Others.title: Pentagon Inks Deals with Nvidia, Microsoft, and AWS to Deploy AI on Classified Networks
Others.description: The U.S. Defense Department signed deals with Nvidia, Microsoft, Amazon Web Services, and Reflection AI to deploy their AI tech on classified networks (IL6 and IL7) for 'lawful operational use.' Over 1.3 million DOD personnel have used GenAI.mil for non-classified tasks. These deals follow controversial disputes with Anthropic over usage terms - Anthropic insisted on guardrails against domestic mass surveillance and autonomous weapons, leading to ongoing legal action. The Pentagon is diversifying AI vendors to prevent lock-in.
Others.author: Ram Iyer

Others.title: UK AI Security Institute Evaluates GPT-5.5 Cyber Capabilities
Others.description: The UK's AI Security Institute evaluated GPT-5.5 for finding security vulnerabilities, finding it comparable to Anthropic's Claude Mythos. Unlike Mythos, GPT-5.5 is generally available now, raising concerns about widespread access to advanced cyber capabilities.
Others.author: Simon Willison

Others.title: Zig Creator Andrew Kelley on Detecting LLM-Assisted Code
Others.description: Zig creator Andrew Kelley explains that LLM-assisted PRs have a 'digital smell' that's obvious to those who don't use AI assistance. He compares it to a smoker entering a room - while smokers don't notice it, non-smokers instantly detect it. Zig maintains a strict ban on LLM-authored contributions.
Others.author: Andrew Kelley (via Simon Willison)

Others.title: Bun's 4x Performance Improvement Can't Be Upstreamed Due to Zig's AI Ban
Others.description: Bun achieved a 4x performance improvement after adding parallel semantic analysis to their Zig fork, but won't upstream it due to Zig's ban on LLM-authored contributions. Bun was acquired by Anthropic in December 2025 and makes heavy use of AI assistance.
Others.author: Simon Willison

Others.title: AI Will Not Replace Programmers But Augment Their Capabilities
Others.description: Industry consensus in 2026 emphasizes that AI will not replace programmers but will augment their capabilities. Developers are advised to focus on learning to work effectively with AI agents while maintaining classic software engineering principles.
Others.author: Industry Experts

Others.title: Agents need control flow, not more prompts
Others.description: A Hacker News discussion (183 points) on a blog post arguing that AI agents need better control flow mechanisms rather than more prompting. This reflects a growing consensus in the AI coding community about the limitations of prompt-based approaches and the need for more structured agent architectures.
Others.author: bsuh (original author)

Others.title: AlphaEvolve: Gemini-powered coding agent scaling impact across fields
Others.description: Google DeepMind's AlphaEvolve (205 points on HN) showcases a Gemini-powered coding agent that scales its impact across multiple fields. This demonstrates the growing trend of domain-specific AI coding agents that can adapt to different programming domains.
Others.author: Google DeepMind

Others.title: DeepSeek 4 Flash local inference engine for Metal
Others.description: A DeepSeek 4 Flash local inference engine for Metal (185 points on HN) by antirez. This enables efficient local running of DeepSeek models on Apple Silicon, relevant to developers who want to run AI coding models locally for privacy or performance reasons.
Others.author: antirez (Salvatore Sanfilippo)

Others.title: Principles for agent-native CLIs
Others.description: Discussion (29 points on HN) about principles for building command-line interfaces that are native to AI agents. As AI coding agents become more prevalent, CLI tools need to be designed with agent interaction in mind, not just human interaction.
Others.author: trevin

Others.title: Show HN: TRUST – Coding Rust like it's 1989
Others.description: A Show HN post (93 points) about TRUST, a Rust coding project. While not directly about AI coding, it reflects ongoing innovation in programming languages and tools that AI coding agents need to understand and work with.
Others.author: wojtczyk

Others.title: AI Slop Is Killing Online Communities
Others.description: A widely-discussed article (172 points on HN) about how AI-generated low-quality content ('slop') is damaging online communities. This raises important questions about the impact of AI coding tools on code quality and the software development ecosystem.
Others.author: rmoff

Others.title: Show HN: Stage CLI – An easier way of reading your AI generated changes locally
Others.description: A Show HN post (24 points) about Stage CLI, a tool for reviewing AI-generated code changes locally. This addresses the growing need for better tools to review and understand code changes made by AI coding agents.
Others.author: cpan22

Others.title: Vibe coding and agentic engineering are getting closer than I'd like
Others.description: Simon Willison discusses how the line between 'vibe coding' (AI coding without understanding) and 'agentic engineering' (responsible AI-assisted development) is blurring. He realizes he's no longer reviewing every line of code Claude writes, treating AI agents like trusted external teams. Explores the normalization of deviance, new challenges in evaluating software quality, shifting bottlenecks in the development lifecycle, and why he's still not concerned for his career. Key insight: Real-world usage is now more valuable than test coverage when evaluating software.
Others.author: Simon Willison

Others.title: SmartBear and Multi-Agent QA
Others.description: Discussion on how AI coding tools have dramatically accelerated development pace and shifted bottlenecks in the software development lifecycle. Covers multi-agent QA systems and the evolving landscape of AI-assisted quality assurance.
Others.author: Software Engineering Daily

Others.title: So you've heard these AI terms and nodded along; let's fix that
Others.description: Comprehensive glossary explaining common AI terminology including concepts like hallucinations, tokens, fine-tuning, RAG (retrieval-augmented generation), and other jargon that has emerged with the rise of large language models. The article serves as an educational resource for developers and non-technical readers trying to navigate AI discourse.
Others.author: TechCrunch Staff

Others.title: Notes on WebRTC prompt degradation
Others.description: Technical critique of WebRTC's aggressive packet dropping behavior during poor network conditions. Willison argues that for expensive LLM prompts, users would prefer higher latency over accuracy loss, but WebRTC's hard-coded implementation prevents waiting or retransmission. This highlights infrastructure challenges in voice-based AI interactions.
Others.author: Simon Willison

Others.title: PlayStation sees AI as a 'powerful tool' to help make games
Others.description: Sony's PlayStation division is actively integrating AI-powered animation tools into game development studios, with Naughty Dog and Santa Monica Studio already adopting the technology. This reflects the growing trend of major game studios using AI to streamline workflows and improve development efficiency.
Others.author: Jay Peters

Others.title: Using Claude Code: The Unreasonable Effectiveness of HTML
Others.description: Simon Willison explores Thariq Shihipar's argument for requesting HTML output from Claude instead of Markdown. While Markdown was previously preferred for token efficiency, HTML enables richer outputs including SVG diagrams, interactive widgets, and in-page navigation. Willison demonstrates this by having GPT-5.5 create an interactive HTML explanation of the copy.fail Linux security exploit, showing how HTML format allows for more comprehensive and navigable technical documentation.
Others.author: Simon Willison

Others.title: Nanoleaf bets its future on robots, red light therapy, and AI
Others.description: Smart lighting company Nanoleaf is pivoting beyond its core business to invest in robotics and AI-powered products. CEO Gimmy Chu explains that commoditization of smart lighting is driving the company's strategic shift toward AI-driven home automation and robotic solutions.
Others.author: Jennifer Pattison Tuohy

Others.title: Databricks Has a Trick That Lets AI Models Improve Themselves
Others.description: Databricks has developed a technique enabling AI models to improve their own performance without requiring extensive human labeling or retraining. The approach leverages synthetic data generation and self-evaluation mechanisms, potentially reducing the cost and time required to enhance model accuracy and capabilities.
Others.author: Will Knight

Others.title: The battle over AI data centers
Others.description: Comprehensive analysis of the growing infrastructure demands of AI development, examining the race to build specialized data centers capable of training and deploying massive AI models. The coverage explores energy consumption, geographic distribution, and the geopolitical implications of AI computing infrastructure.
Others.author: Verge Staff and Justine Calma

Others.title: Cloudflare is laying off 1,100 workers as its AI usage increases by 600 percent
Others.description: Cloudflare announced it's reducing its workforce by 1,100 employees while reporting a 600% increase in AI usage. The company stated these actions are about redefining how a high-growth company operates in the 'agentic AI era,' highlighting how AI automation is transforming workforce dynamics even at tech companies scaling their AI capabilities.
Others.author: Emma Roth

Others.title: AI evaluation startup Braintrust confirms breach, tells every customer to rotate sensitive keys
Others.description: AI evaluation platform Braintrust confirmed a security breach and has advised all customers to rotate their sensitive API keys and credentials. The incident highlights growing security concerns around AI developer tools that store and process sensitive authentication data for multiple AI services.
Others.author: Lorenzo Franceschi-Bicchierai

Others.title: Boston Dynamics Led a Robot Revolution. Now Its Machines Are Teaching Themselves New Tricks
Others.description: Boston Dynamics is transitioning from pre-programmed robot behaviors to machine learning approaches that enable robots to learn new skills autonomously. The shift represents a fundamental change in robotics development, moving away from hand-coded control systems toward AI-driven learning and adaptation.
Others.author: Will Knight

Others.title: Local AI Needs to Be the Norm - Hacker News Discussion
Others.description: A Hacker News discussion (438 points) on the importance of running AI models locally. The discussion emphasizes privacy, data sovereignty, and reducing dependence on cloud services. This reflects growing sentiment in the developer community about local-first AI development.
Others.author: Hacker News Community

Others.title: Task Paralysis and AI - Hacker News Discussion
Others.description: A popular Hacker News thread (185 points) discussing how AI tools affect productivity and task management. The conversation explores whether AI assistants help overcome task paralysis or contribute to it, with developers sharing personal experiences about AI's impact on their workflow.
Others.author: Hacker News Community

Others.title: Y Combinator's Stake in OpenAI Revealed
Others.description: John Gruber revealed that Y Combinator owns approximately 0.6% of OpenAI, which at OpenAI's current $852 billion valuation is worth over $5 billion. This information was difficult to obtain and came from sources familiar with OpenAI investors.
Others.author: John Gruber (covered by Simon Willison)

Others.title: AI Code Generation Adoption Exceeds 85% in 2026
Others.description: Reports indicate that AI code generation adoption has exceeded 85% in 2026. The market is shifting from simple code completion to full-process automation. Key trends include: Agentic Coding era where AI evolves from helpers to engineering participants, enterprise-grade security becoming a priority, and multi-scenario tool specialization for enterprise vs. individual vs. cloud-native development.
Others.author: Various Industry Reports

Others.title: 2026 AI Programming Tools Competitive Landscape Shifting
Others.description: The AI programming tools market in 2026 is led by Cursor, GitHub Copilot, and Windsurf, with emerging open-source Coding Agent projects gaining traction. The landscape now includes four major categories: terminal-native agents, IDE extension plugins, AI-native IDE forks, and complex engineering orchestration platforms.
Others.author: 51CTO
